situation:
You are the human resources manager at LOCKSTONE LOGISTICS GROUP, a warehousing and freight company that merged with PENNYCROSS WAREHOUSING nine months ago. The senior vice president (judge) has asked to meet you about the integration plan waiting for a decision.

Nine months on, the two halves still run as two companies. LOCKSTONE schedules its warehouses centrally. PENNYCROSS never did: its crews swap shifts among themselves and rearrange the day around a customer who calls with a late order, and the accounts that came over in the merger say that responsiveness is what they were buying. Customers were told the two systems would be one by year's end, and the company is carrying both.

The integration plan puts every site on the central schedule. It ends the duplicate systems and the two pay scales, and it also ends the crew-run shift swapping that the former PENNYCROSS employees name, in every exit interview and every stay conversation, as the reason they stay. Those same crews filed for a union election last month, and the vote is six weeks away.

Standardizing now would capture the savings the merger was sold on, and it would take away the practice those crews say keeps them here, in the weeks before their vote, where it will be read as an answer to the campaign. Holding the plan until after the vote would leave the practice and the goodwill in place, and the company would go on paying for two scheduling systems and two pay scales it told customers would be gone by year's end.

The senior vice president (judge) wants your recommendation on what LOCKSTONE does with the integration plan and when, how the work those crews do is recognized either way, and what the company is competing on if the responsiveness the accounts came for goes. You will present to the senior vice president (judge), who will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the senior vice president (judge) of LOCKSTONE LOGISTICS GROUP. Business background is the same as the situation above. The integration plan would put every site on the central schedule and end the duplicate systems and the two pay scales, the former PENNYCROSS crews say the crew-run shift swapping is why they stay, and their union election is six weeks away.

You have asked the human resources manager to recommend what the company does with the integration plan and when, how the work those crews do is recognized either way, and what LOCKSTONE is competing on if the responsiveness the merged accounts came for goes.

After the participant has presented, ask these questions:
judgeQuestions: A year after we do this, what changes that we are not expecting today?
